decisions.reason: As a low-cost plugin very close to the core shop optimization offer, it preserves an option on further demand while one year of market presence reveals too little negative evidence to justify exit.

Because an ERP interface deepens integration with clients' shop operations and fits the firm's move toward broader multichannel support, management would keep this strategically valuable option open absent clear signs of failure.

A price comparison tracking plugin is adjacent to the firm's analytics and marketing capabilities, and with limited time on the market and likely modest carrying costs it is rational to continue learning rather than abandon it early.

Given the firm's growth, in-house development capacity and the product's close fit with measurable marketing services, keeping this plugin is the better real-options choice while uncertainty about adoption remains unresolved.

Since this plugin extends an established service area and there is no evidence yet that its value is unlikely to materialize, the firm would keep the option alive rather than redeploy resources prematurely.

A net price reporting plugin complements the firm's technical and analytics-oriented ecommerce support, and its proximity to the core business makes continued offering a low-risk way to retain upside under uncertainty.
